---
title: Chinese Civil War Soldiers
---

<p>In the nineteenth century, Chinese men fought in the American Civil War—yet their presence has largely remained absent from its historical narrative. Their lives survive only in fragments across enlistment records, census schedules, pension files, and scattered references in newspapers. This project reconstructs those lives, tracing how Chinese men participated in the war and what that participation reveals about race, citizenship, and belonging in the United States.</p>

<p>Through soldier profiles, thematic essays, and digital mapping, the project examines three interconnected questions. First, what did it mean for Chinese men to fight for a nation that did not fully recognize them as citizens? Second, how did military service place them within bureaucratic systems that recorded and classified their identities? And third, how were they perceived by the Americans around them, and how did those perceptions shape the possibilities available to them? Taken together, these perspectives reveal Civil War participation not as a simple marker of inclusion, but as part of an ongoing process of negotiation shaped by race, institutions, and public discourse.</p>

<p>This project builds on work preserved by the <a href="https://www.nps.gov/" target="_blank">National Park Service</a> and other archival institutions.</p>
